What degraded

  • The voting hours on frame 9 and in the caption are Harris County's only. League City also lies in Galveston County, whose Election Day hours were not in the record; both surfaces name the two counties so the hours read as Harris County's.
  • The local suite's clone step failed on the container's system Pillow; the steps this run touched were run one by one by exit code, and CI is the full check.
  • The webapi.legistar.com API answered 500 for part of the run; every quote was checked against the copy saved earlier in the run.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Fixed locations on public roadways, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

A "nonbinding" no would reach League City's cameras.

The word is the ballot's. On Harris County's sample ballot, Proposition A asks "As a nonbinding statement of voter preference" whether police should keep the fixed plate reader cameras. The council added the word on August 11th. League City lies in Galveston and Harris counties. Harris County vote centers take voters from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3rd.

The council's own record goes further. On October 13th it passed Resolution No. 2026-185 by 8 to 0. It directs removal of the fixed cameras if a majority rejects their continued use. Mayor Nick Long told the council "there's no second vote needed," the Tribune reported.

By the Tribune's account Long put the start of bagging at 72 hours after certification. If a majority votes no Tuesday, when will the count be certified?

#LeagueCity #GalvestonCounty #PropositionA

The machine changed itself

  • Kit: road paint added to the civic family, at the fix the judges named
    A crosswalk bar is now a 7 mm bevelled extrusion with a bead-white top that casts under a low key, and a raised marker's reflector is warm facets rather than a mirror of the navy sky. Proved in close renders at the deck's own light (commit 1ad5952a).
  • Gate: the sources block fails a document label with a non-ordinal date or the post's own year
    Three of this week's five decks shipped that defect or nearly did, and only no. 64's was caught, by a judge (commit aef54b75).
  • Proposals needing a maintainer
    The engine id pass (the queue's GRID count at repeat 5 and two accent items at repeat 2, all met today), a GATE_LESSONS entry for the new rule, and prompt_audit counting agent spawns as permission waits (daily lane, repeat 2). In UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md, 2026-10-31.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record first. Re-verify (commit 881ba8dc) fetched 49 urls behind 180 claims. tx-2026-0150 and tx-2026-0151 were repointed to PubMed and stamped, 27 items carry a dated unconfirmed line and 26 boundaries were re-measured. tx-2026-0235, Pflugerville's SAFE technology standards (RES-1443), was admitted on the city's Legistar record. tx-2026-0048 gained League City's October 13th resolution directing removal of the fixed plate reader cameras if voters reject them, its vote rows and the privacy committee ordinance (commit 4d0a6809). The deck. Carousel no. 64 is League City's Proposition A, drawn as road paint at one corner: one stripe, marker, bar or groove per camera, agency, recorded vote or hour, each counted from the record. It shipped at the round cap at 7.366, 0.634 under the 8.0 top rung, with no hard fail across three panel rounds (7.29, 7.434, 7.366). The art median of 6.8 is under the 8.5 craft floor, which stands down at the cap. The judges still charge frame 7's crosswalk tops reading as brown planks, frame 5's bars showing no cast, frame 4's marker field as wallpaper and frame 8 as a grille. Before posting. The cover says League City votes Tuesday, so it is right only if the post goes out before November 3rd. Variety. The thirty day rule clears tx-2026-0048, but three judges charged variety: no. 4 (August 20th) was this same item and no. 39 (October 1st) named the vote and the Kyle and Laredo referendums. Corrections the panel forced, each checked against the record. The resolution's own title reads "directing removal". Frame 8 now discloses both press accounts of the 72 hours (the Tribune's "start bagging 72 hours after certification" and Houston Public Media's "down within 72 hours"). Frame 3 was rebuilt so 55 measures 55/70 of the 70, and the 55 is attributed as the figure the Tribune reports. Did the run stop for a human. The interim reading before the merge measured 1,962 tool calls and flagged 188 as waiting, led by Agent and SendMessage dispatches of 6 to 29 seconds and Bash at about one second. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:06:52 UTC, judged the session unattended from its first call with the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, and refused nothing. The waits read as dispatch latency, the queued prompt-audit-counts-agent-latency item. The machine. Six queue items were raised and three added. With two repeat offenders the weekly pass came due and ran before the merge; its changes are listed under the machine heading.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
